data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 claims formal verification 'eliminates hidden correlations by fiat,' but formal verification cannot verify the correctness of its own assumptions relative to the real world. The mechanism conflates formal-internal isolation (proved under a spec) with de facto independence of failure modes. A shared spec flaw, shared environmental assumption, or shared compiler/kernel CVE outside the verification boundary can still correlate all isolation domains simultaneously. The target's own disanalogy admits this ('assumptions may be incomplete'), yet the claim still asserts elimination of hidden correlations. This is a causal-mechanism failure: the stated mechanism does not causally produce the claimed independence.
